seoulCurated.intro: Guidebook-style day itineraries for Seoul. Pick a title to read the overview, route outline, and timetable.

c01.title: Gyeongbokgung · Bukchon · Insadong
c01.summary: A classic Seoul day: palace grounds, hanok alleys, Insadong crafts, Ikseon café vibes…
c01.route: Gyeongbokgung → Bukchon → Insadong → Ikseondong → Gwangjang Market → Cheonggyecheon
c01.tips: Wearing hanbok often means free palace entry. Bukchon is residential—keep voices down and be mindful when photographing.

stops.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
stops.desc: Tour Geunjeongjeon and Gyeonghoeru at an easy pace.

stops.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
stops.desc: Walk the tiled rooftops and viewpoint alleys of Gahoe-dong.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Tea houses, bibimbap, and Korean set menus.

stops.name: Ssamziegil & Insadong street
stops.desc: Browse crafts, souvenirs, and street snacks along gallery-lined alleys.

stops.name: Ikseondong café
stops.desc: Hanok cafés and bakeries for an afternoon dessert break.

stops.name: Gwangjang Market
stops.desc: Try mayak gimbap, bindaetteok, and yukhoe—share a few plates before…

stops.name: Cheonggyecheon walk
stops.desc: End with an easy waterside walk and night lights.

c02.title: Myeongdong · Namsan · City center
c02.summary: Shopping plus skyline views: Myeongdong, Namsan & N Seoul Tower, Namdaemun Market…
c02.route: Myeongdong → Namsan → N Seoul Tower → Namdaemun Market → Seoul Station / Seoullo
c02.tips: Sunset and night views at N Seoul Tower are popular—budget time for cable car or bus queues.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: From kalguksu to global chains—try side alleys if main streets are…

stops.name: Namsan walk
stops.desc: Take the loop road or walk up toward the tower; on clear days walking…

stops.name: N Seoul Tower
stops.desc: City panorama from the observatory—golden hour is great for photos.

stops.name: Namdaemun Market
stops.desc: Clothes, household goods, and market meals like grilled fish or noodles.

stops.name: Seoul Station · Seoullo 7017
stops.desc: Pause on the elevated park for skyline views around sunset.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Return to Myeongdong or chase neon alleys and old-school eateries in…

c03.title: Seongsu · Seoul Forest
c03.summary: Green park mornings, Seongsu cafés and pop-ups, then Hangang vibes and a Konkuk…
c03.route: Seoul Forest → Seongsu → Ttukseom Hangang Park → Konkuk Univ. area
c03.tips: Weekend afternoons in Seongsu are crowded—go early or on weekdays for cafés.

stops.name: Seoul Forest
stops.desc: Start on the lawns and paths; bike rentals are available.

stops.name: Seongsu café streets
stops.desc: Converted warehouses, bakeries, and concept stores near Seongsu Station.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Brunch and casual kitchens—arrive early for popular spots.

stops.name: Pop-ups & shops
stops.desc: Seasonal pop-ups and design stores; check what’s on before you go.

stops.name: Ttukseom Hangang Park
stops.desc: Nearby river park for bikes, picnics, and sunset photos.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Casual chicken, gopchang, and Asian eats around the station.

stops.name: Konkuk streets at night
stops.desc: Wander the lit shopping streets to wrap up.

c04.title: Hongdae · Yeonnam · Mangwon
c04.summary: Yeonnam alleys, Hongdae street energy, Mangwon Market snacks, and Hangang sunset—then…
c04.route: Yeonnam → Hongdae → Mangwon Market → Mangwon Hangang Park → Hongdae
c04.tips: Hongdae peaks at night. Use station lockers if you’re carrying shopping bags.

stops.name: Yeonnam-dong
stops.desc: Quiet cafés and shops; add Gyeongui Line Forest Park if you like a…

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Brunch spots fill up on weekends—aim for opening time.

stops.name: Hongdae streets
stops.desc: Busking, murals, and street fashion—easy to lose track of time.

stops.name: Cafés & shopping
stops.desc: Vintage, beauty, and lifestyle stores with coffee breaks in between.

stops.name: Mangwon Market
stops.desc: Local market bites—pack some snacks for the river if you like.

stops.name: Mangwon Hangang Park
stops.desc: Sunset breeze, bikes, and picnic vibes.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Return for dinner, neon streets, and nightlife.

c05.title: Gangnam · Jamsil
c05.summary: COEX and Starfield Library, Bongeunsa Temple, then Seokchon Lake, Lotte World Mall…
c05.route: COEX → Bongeunsa → Seokchon Lake → Lotte World Mall → Seoul Sky
c05.tips: COEX to Bongeunsa is a short walk. Book Seoul Sky for night views if you can.

stops.name: COEX
stops.desc: Mall, aquarium, and indoor events—good weather backup.

stops.name: Starfield Library
stops.desc: Iconic book-wall photo stop; a short visit is enough.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Food court or nearby restaurants before the temple.

stops.name: Bongeunsa
stops.desc: A calm temple framed by glass towers.

stops.name: Transfer to Jamsil
stops.desc: About 15–25 minutes on Line 2 toward Jamsil/Seokchon.

stops.name: Seokchon Lake
stops.desc: Lakeside walk with Lotte Tower in the background.

stops.name: Lotte World Mall
stops.desc: Shopping, aquarium, and easy dinner options under one roof.

stops.name: Seoul Sky or Jamsil night view
stops.desc: Observatory views—or enjoy the tower lights from the lake.

c06.title: Dongdaemun · Daehangno
c06.summary: Naksan views, Daehangno theater streets, DDP architecture, Dongdaemun shopping, then…
c06.route: Naksan Park → Daehangno → DDP → Dongdaemun → Gwangjang Market → Cheonggyecheon
c06.tips: Walk the fortress wall at Naksan. DDP looks especially good after dark.

stops.name: Naksan Park
stops.desc: City views along the old city wall—soft morning light is lovely.

stops.name: Ihwa Mural Village · Daehangno
stops.desc: Murals plus indie theaters and café streets.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Student-friendly prices: cutlets, soups, and global casual food.

stops.name: Transfer to Dongdaemun
stops.desc: Subway or bus toward DDP and the fashion district.

stops.name: DDP
stops.desc: Explore the curved design plaza and any open exhibitions.

stops.name: Dongdaemun shopping
stops.desc: Fashion malls by day; night-market energy after dark.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Market classics for a hearty evening—go early on weekends.

c07.title: Hangang · Yeouido
c07.summary: Shop The Hyundai Seoul, then spend the afternoon on Yeouido Hangang Park with bikes, a…
c07.route: The Hyundai Seoul → Yeouido Park → Yeouido Hangang Park → Hangang night view
c07.tips: Reserve river cruises ahead. A picnic mat makes the park much more comfortable.

stops.name: The Hyundai Seoul
stops.desc: A huge lifestyle mall—start slow in the morning.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Mall restaurants or Yeouido business-district kitchens.

stops.name: Yeouido Hangang Park
stops.desc: Grass, bike paths, and skyline views—rent a bike if you can.

stops.name: Café break by the river
stops.desc: Coffee from a park café or convenience store, then sit by the water.

stops.name: Cruise or long walk
stops.desc: Take a Hangang cruise or simply walk until sunset.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Eat near the park or National Assembly area.

stops.name: Hangang night view
stops.desc: Bridge lights reflecting on the river.

c08.title: Seochon · Gwanghwamun
c08.summary: Palace morning, Seochon hanok cafés, Gwanghwamun Square, then Cheonggyecheon and…
c08.tips: Seochon is usually quieter than Bukchon. Tiny cafés may have waits.

stops.name: Gyeongbokgung
stops.desc: Arrive at opening for lighter crowds; check gate routes in advance.

stops.name: Seochon
stops.desc: Tongin/Okin hanok lanes with workshops and galleries.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Korean homes-style spots and café brunch tucked in alleys.

stops.name: Café alley stroll
stops.desc: Dessert stops and craft shops at a slow pace.

stops.name: Gwanghwamun Square
stops.desc: Gate views, statues, and the open plaza.

stops.name: Euljiro
stops.desc: Print shops, old diners, and trendy bars share the same alleys.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Classic Korean taverns or cocktail bars to close the day.

c09.title: Itaewon · Hannam
c09.summary: Hannam’s polished cafés and boutiques, then Itaewon, Gyeongnidan-gil, Haebangchon…
c09.tips: Expect hills—wear comfortable shoes. Weekends get busy after dark.

stops.name: Hannam-dong
stops.desc: Upscale cafés, galleries, and concept stores—best by day.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Brunch and global restaurants; reservations help.

stops.name: Itaewon
stops.desc: International streets for people-watching and shopping.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Characterful restaurants and bars in steep alleys.

stops.name: Namsan night views
stops.desc: Catch the skyline from Namsan’s lower paths or viewpoints.

c10.title: Markets & food trail
c10.summary: A food-first day linking Namdaemun, Myeongdong, Gwangjang, Ikseon, Jongno, and…
c10.route: Namdaemun Market → Myeongdong → Gwangjang Market → Ikseondong → Jongno → Cheonggyecheon
c10.tips: Most stalls take cards, but tiny stands may prefer cash.

stops.name: Namdaemun Market
stops.desc: Start with market energy—noodles and small bites work well.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Sit-down market restaurants; shared tables are common.

stops.name: Myeongdong
stops.desc: Digest with shopping and street desserts.

stops.name: Gwangjang Market
stops.desc: Round two: yukhoe, bindaetteok, and savory pancakes.

stops.name: Ikseondong
stops.desc: Hanok cafés for a sweet pause.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Izakaya-style and Korean pubs near Jongno/Ikseon.

c11.title: Jamsil · Songridan-gil
c11.summary: Lotte World Mall, Seokchon Lake, Songridan-gil cafés, and Seoul Sky—all in the Jamsil…
c11.route: Lotte World Mall → Seokchon Lake → Songridan-gil → Seoul Sky
c11.tips: Songridan-gil sits on the east side of the lake—pair a full lake loop with café time.

stops.name: Seokchon Lake
stops.desc: Scenic walk with tower views; beautiful in every season.

stops.name: Seoul Sky
stops.desc: Observatory views—enter near sunset if possible.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Eat back at the mall or around Jamsil Station.

c12.title: Hangang · Banpo
c12.summary: Express Bus Terminal & Seorae village vibes, Some Sevit, Banpo Hangang Park picnic…
c12.route: Express Bus Terminal → Some Sevit → Banpo Hangang Park
c12.tips: The Banpo Moonlight Rainbow Fountain schedule changes by season—check before you go.

stops.name: Express Bus Terminal · Parnie Station area
stops.desc: Mall and café complex to start the day.

stops.name: Some Sevit
stops.desc: Floating islands on the Hangang—great exterior photos.

stops.name: Banpo Hangang Park
stops.desc: Bikes, walks, and picnics with easy convenience stores nearby.

stops.name: Hangang picnic
stops.desc: Snacks and sunset on the grass.

stops.name: Night view & fountain
stops.desc: Bridge lights and the fountain show when operating.

c13.title: Yongsan · Ichon
c13.summary: National Museum of Korea, Yongsan lunch, Yongridan-gil cafés, then Ichon Hangang Park.
c13.route: National Museum of Korea → Yongsan → Yongridan-gil → Ichon Hangang Park
c13.tips: The museum is huge—pick highlights. Check closed days for special exhibits.

stops.name: National Museum of Korea
stops.desc: History and art collections plus outdoor gardens.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Yongsan Station / I’Park Mall dining options.

stops.name: Yongridan-gil
stops.desc: Cafés and restaurants near the electronics market area.

stops.name: Cafés & shopping
stops.desc: Slow café hopping and lifestyle stores.

stops.name: Ichon Hangang Park
stops.desc: River walk and bikes with soft sunset light.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Stay in Yongsan or drift toward Itaewon for dinner.

c14.title: Northern Seoul · Seongbuk-dong
c14.summary: Quiet Seongbuk-dong lanes, Gilseongsa Temple, Bukjeong village cafés, then dinner in…
c14.tips: Expect slopes—comfortable shoes and a relaxed pace help.

stops.name: Hansung Univ. Station area
stops.desc: Gateway toward Seongbuk-dong by bus or taxi.

stops.name: Seongbuk-dong stroll
stops.desc: Stone walls, embassies, and quiet hanok streets.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Eat in Seongbuk-dong or nearby Hyehwa.

stops.name: Gilseongsa
stops.desc: A peaceful temple pocket in the city.

stops.name: Bukjeong Village · cafés
stops.desc: Hill views and photo-friendly café corners.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Plenty of casual restaurants to end the day.

c15.title: Seoul Forest · Hangang · Apgujeong
c15.summary: From Seoul Forest and Seongsu into Apgujeong Rodeo and Dosan Park for a polished…
c15.route: Seoul Forest → Seongsu → Apgujeong Rodeo → Dosan Park
c15.tips: Seongsu to Apgujeong is an easy subway/taxi hop. Book dinner around Dosan if you’re set on a popular spot.

stops.name: Seoul Forest
stops.desc: Morning walk and photos before Seongsu fills up.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Brunch or lunch at a Seongsu favorite.

stops.name: Apgujeong Rodeo
stops.desc: Fashion and beauty streets for window shopping.

stops.name: Dosan Park
stops.desc: A green pause with galleries and cafés nearby.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Stylish restaurants and bars to close the night.

curated.intro: A guidebook of signature courses for this region. When they are added, pick a title to see the intro, route, and timetable.

gyeonggi.intro: Day courses around Gyeonggi—Suwon, Gapyeong, Paju, Everland, the Korean Folk Village, Yangpyeong, Gwangmyeong, Namhansanseong, Pocheon, and Yeoju. Pick a title to see the intro, route, and timetable.

c01.title: Suwon Hwaseong · Haenggung-dong
c01.summary: UNESCO Hwaseong and Haenggung, lunch and cafés in Haenggung-dong, then Banghwasuryujeong and fortress lights. Easy by subway and bus.
c01.route: Hwaseong Fortress → Hwaseong Haenggung → Haenggung-dong → Banghwasuryujeong
c01.tips: The wall walk is long—wear comfortable shoes. Suwon Station and Haenggung are easy by subway and bus.

stops.name: Suwon Hwaseong
stops.desc: Walk the walls around Janganmun and Paldalmun for fortress views.

stops.name: Hwaseong Haenggung
stops.desc: Jeongjo’s temporary palace—tour the main halls at an easy pace.

stops.name: Haenggung-dong lunch
stops.desc: Korean meals and snacks in the alleys in front of the palace.

stops.name: Haengnidangil
stops.desc: Cafés and small shops in the lanes east of the palace.

stops.name: Banghwasuryujeong
stops.desc: Northeast pavilion and Yongyeon pond; beautiful near sunset.

stops.name: Hwaseong night views
stops.desc: Finish with a slow walk along the lit fortress walls.

c02.title: Gapyeong highlights
c02.summary: Nami Island, then Petite France and the Italian Village, finishing at the Garden of Morning Calm. A car (or tour van) makes the hops easy.
c02.route: Nami Island → Petite France → Garden of Morning Calm
c02.tips: Allow ferry-queue time at Nami. Check seasonal hours for the garden. Linking all three by transit alone is tight.

stops.name: Nami Island
stops.desc: Metasequoia lane, bikes, and riverside paths at an easy pace.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Eat on the island or near the Gapyeong pier.

stops.name: Garden of Morning Calm
stops.desc: Themed gardens and trails—check last entry.

stops.name: Finish
stops.desc: End at the garden and head back toward Seoul or Chuncheon.

c03.title: Paju DMZ course
c03.summary: Imjingak Peace Nuri, a DMZ tour, then a slower afternoon in Heyri Art Village. A car or reserved tour is the practical way.
c03.tips: DMZ sites usually need a passport and advance booking. Walk-up tickets can sell out. Wear comfortable shoes.

stops.name: Imjingak Peace Nuri
stops.desc: Freedom Bridge, prayer ribbons, and the park—start with the border story.

stops.name: DMZ tour
stops.desc: Dora Observatory, the Third Tunnel, and the day’s circuit. A guided tour is the safer option.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Eat at Imjingak or in Paju town.

stops.name: Café
stops.desc: A slow café stop in Heyri.

stops.name: Finish
stops.desc: Head back toward Seoul before dark.

c03.notice: DMZ sites change reservation, ID, and entry rules often. Check Gyeonggi Tourism and the site itself before you go.

c04.title: Everland day
c04.summary: A full day inside Everland: safari and rides, gardens, dinner, then the parade and night shows—no extra destinations.
c04.tips: On weekends, arrive at opening. Parade times change by season. Everline, shuttles, or a car all work.

stops.name: Enter Everland
stops.desc: Arrive at opening and check wait times and a walking loop.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Garden food court or a themed restaurant.

stops.name: Safari & rides
stops.desc: Safari World and headline attractions in the afternoon.

stops.name: Gardens & more rides
stops.desc: Four Seasons Garden and anything you skipped.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Eat in the park and claim a night-show spot.

stops.name: Parade & night shows
stops.desc: Seasonal parade, lights, and closing entertainment.

c05.title: Korean Folk Village course
c05.summary: Traditional houses, shows, and crafts at the Korean Folk Village, then Bojeong café street in the evening.
c05.route: Korean Folk Village → Bojeong café street
c05.tips: Give the village at least half a day. Check the performance board at the gate. Bojeong is near Jukjeon and Bojeong on the Bundang Line.

stops.name: Korean Folk Village
stops.desc: An open-air Joseon village—start with houses and the market lane.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Traditional Korean meals inside the village.

stops.name: Shows & workshops
stops.desc: Pick the day’s nongak, tightrope, or craft sessions.

stops.name: Leave the village
stops.desc: Exit before dusk and move to Bojeong.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Casual dinner around Bojeong or Jukjeon.

c05.notice: DMZ sites often require advance booking, ID, and changing entry rules. Check Gyeonggi Tourism and the facility before you go.

c06.title: Yangpyeong Dumulmeori course
c06.summary: Dumulmeori and Semiwon, then a riverside café and a Namhangang walk. Spread out—easier by car.
c06.tips: Dumulmeori is busy weekend mornings. Semiwon’s lotus peaks in summer. Riverside cafés often have tight parking.

stops.name: Dumulmeori
stops.desc: Where the Bukhangang and Namhangang meet—photo spots and paths.

stops.name: Semiwon
stops.desc: Lotus ponds, water gardens, and boardwalks.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Korean restaurants near Dumulmeori or Semiwon.

stops.name: Riverside café
stops.desc: A slow coffee with a Namhangang view.

stops.name: Namhangang walk
stops.desc: An easy stroll along the river.

stops.name: Finish
stops.desc: Head back toward Seoul before dark.

c07.title: Gwangmyeong Cave course
c07.summary: Gwangmyeong Cave, then the traditional market and downtown cafés. Workable by subway and bus.
c07.route: Gwangmyeong Cave → Gwangmyeong Traditional Market → downtown
c07.tips: The cave is cool and floors can be damp. The market sits near Cheolsan Station. Link cave and market by bus or taxi.

stops.name: Gwangmyeong Cave
stops.desc: A former mine turned attraction—Golden Waterfall, wine cellar, and light art.

stops.name: Gwangmyeong Traditional Market
stops.desc: Food and side streets around Cheolsan.

stops.name: Finish
stops.desc: Back to Seoul from Cheolsan or Gwangmyeong Station.

c08.title: Namhansanseong course
c08.summary: UNESCO fortress walls, a village lunch, more ramparts, then a café. Reachable by bus from Seoul.
c08.tips: Buses reach the fortress. Trails are hilly—wear good shoes. It can be windy when the weather turns.

stops.name: Namhansanseong
stops.desc: UNESCO walls around the south gate.

stops.name: More fortress
stops.desc: West gate, the temporary palace site, and leftover stretches.

stops.name: Café
stops.desc: A café inside the fortress village.

stops.name: Finish
stops.desc: Bus down and back to Seoul.

c09.title: Pocheon nature course
c09.summary: Pocheon Art Valley’s quarry lake, then Sanjeong Lake for a walk and café. You will want a car.
c09.tips: Art Valley charges admission and weekend parking fills up. A full loop of Sanjeong Lake is long. Buses between the two are infrequent.

stops.name: Pocheon Art Valley
stops.desc: A granite quarry turned lake, viewpoints, and sculpture park.

stops.name: Sanjeong Lake
stops.desc: Walk the shore with Myeongseongsan behind the water.

stops.name: Walk · café
stops.desc: A lakeside café or a shorter extra stroll.

stops.name: Finish
stops.desc: Drive back toward Seoul from Pocheon.

c10.title: Yeoju history & shopping
c10.summary: Silleuksa and King Sejong’s tomb, then Yeoju Premium Outlets. Spread out—easier by car.
c10.route: Silleuksa → King Sejong’s tomb → Yeoju Outlet
c10.tips: Silleuksa sits on the Namhangang—pair it with a riverside walk. The outlet gets busy weekend evenings.

stops.name: Namhangang walk
stops.desc: A short stroll in front of the temple.

stops.name: Finish
stops.desc: End at the outlet and drive back.

c11.title: Icheon ceramics course
c11.summary: Yespark (ceramic village) and Cerapia—Icheon’s pottery day. A car helps between sites.
c11.tips: Studios may need a booking for hands-on sessions. Cerapia is mostly outdoors—watch the weather.

stops.name: Icheon Ceramic Village
stops.desc: Walk Yespark’s studio streets and browse pottery.

stops.name: Icheon lunch
stops.desc: Local rice meals and Korean food.

c12.title: Yeoju history & outlet course
c12.summary: Silleuksa and King Sejong’s tomb, then Yeoju Premium Outlets. Spread out—easier by car.
c12.route: Silleuksa → King Sejong’s tomb → Yeoju Outlet
c12.tips: Silleuksa sits on the Namhangang—pair it with a riverside walk. The outlet gets busy weekend evenings.

stops.name: Namhangang walk
stops.desc: A short stroll in front of the temple.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Outlet food hall or Yeoju town.

c13.title: Siheung · Oido course
c13.summary: Gaetgol wetlands, then Oido’s red lighthouse and seafood. Easy on Line 4.
c13.tips: Gaetgol is known for sunset and reeds. Expect waits for grilled clams at dinner.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: A simple meal near the park.

stops.name: Oido
stops.desc: A coastal village at the edge of Siheung.

c14.title: Ansan Daebudo course
c14.summary: Daebudo, Bada Hyanggi Arboretum, and Tando Port sunset. You’ll want a car on the island.
c14.route: Daebudo → Bada Hyanggi Arboretum → Tando Port
c14.tips: Sunset time shifts by season. Weekend parking at Tando fills early.

stops.name: Daebudo
stops.desc: An island linked by the Sihwa seawall—start a coastal drive.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Seafood or Korean meals on the island.

stops.name: Bada Hyanggi Arboretum
stops.desc: An island arboretum with trails and a greenhouse.

stops.name: Tando Port
stops.desc: A small harbor famous for sunset.

stops.name: Sunset
stops.desc: Watch the Yellow Sea from the breakwater.

stops.name: Daebudo dinner
stops.desc: Dinner at the harbor before heading back.

c15.title: Seongnam · Namhansanseong course
c15.summary: Walk UNESCO Namhansanseong, then Pangyo for cafés and dinner—workable by transit.
c15.tips: Buses reach the fortress. Trails are hilly—wear good shoes. Pangyo Station is on the Shinbundang Line.

stops.name: Namhansanseong
stops.desc: UNESCO walls and the fortress village.

stops.name: Wall walk
stops.desc: More ramparts toward the south and west gates.

stops.name: To Pangyo
stops.desc: Bus down, then Shinbundang Line to Pangyo.

stops.name: Hyundai Dept. · Pangyo café
stops.desc: Mall time and Techno Valley cafés.

incheon.intro: Day courses around Incheon—Chinatown, the Open Port, Wolmido, Songdo, Yeongjong, and Ganghwa. Pick a title to see the intro, route, and timetable.

c01.title: Chinatown · Open Port · Wolmido
c01.summary: The classic first-day loop official Incheon tourism promotes: Chinatown and Jayu Park, then the Open Port and Sinpo Market, ending on Wolmido at night. Easy by subway and short taxi hops.
c01.route: Chinatown → Jayu Park → Open Port → Sinpo Market → Wolmido
c01.tips: Incheon Station (Line 1, Suin–Bundang) is next to Chinatown and the Open Port. Use a bus or taxi for Wolmido. Sinpo Market gets busy on weekends.

stops.name: Incheon Chinatown
stops.desc: Walk the lanes around Inhwamun and the street gates.

stops.name: Jayu Park
stops.desc: MacArthur statue and a view over the harbor and Open Port.

stops.name: Chinatown lunch
stops.desc: Jajangmyeon, kungalppang, and other Chinatown staples.

stops.name: Open Port culture district
stops.desc: Western-style modern buildings and museum streets.

stops.name: Sinpo International Market
stops.desc: Sinpo chicken gangjeong and market alleys.

stops.name: Wolmido
stops.desc: Seaside walk, rides, or the Wolmi Sea Train.

stops.name: Wolmido dinner & night view
stops.desc: Eat by the water after the lights come on.

c02.title: Songdo International City
c02.summary: The modern-Korea skyline visitors come to photograph: Central Park and Tri-bowl, Hyundai Premium Outlet, then the park again after dark. Official Incheon tourism lists the park and outlet as Songdo’s headline stops.
c02.route: Central Park → Tri-bowl → Hyundai Premium Outlet → Central Park at night
c02.tips: Incheon Line 1 Central Park Station sits by the park. Bus or taxi is easier for the outlet. Golden hour around the canal is the photo window.

stops.name: Songdo Central Park
stops.desc: Walk the canal paths under the skyline.

stops.name: Tri-bowl & park stroll
stops.desc: The bowl-shaped landmark and more waterfront.

stops.name: Hyundai Premium Outlet
stops.desc: Brand shopping and an indoor break.

stops.name: Central Park again
stops.desc: Return for golden hour on the canal.

stops.name: Songdo night view
stops.desc: Lit towers reflected on the park water.

c03.title: Yeongjong · Eulwangni coast
c03.summary: A beach day that fits a spare day before or after Incheon Airport. Masian Beach and an ocean-view café, then Eulwangni for a walk, sunset, and dinner.
c03.route: Masian Beach → ocean-view café → Eulwangni Beach
c03.tips: Masian sits on Muui-do, linked to Yeongjong by bridge. Hop between beaches by bus or taxi. West Sea tides change the shoreline a lot—check the tide.

stops.name: Masian Beach
stops.desc: A headline beach for the Yeongjong–Muui area. Sand and café streets.

stops.name: Lunch by the beach
stops.desc: Seafood or simple Korean meals along the shore.

stops.name: Ocean-view café
stops.desc: An afternoon looking at the water.

stops.name: Beach walk
stops.desc: The breakwater and sand at an easy pace.

stops.name: Sunset
stops.desc: Wait for the Yellow Sea sunset.

stops.name: Dinner
stops.desc: Grilled clams or other seaside meals.

c04.title: Yeongjong · Paradise City
c04.summary: Paradise City and Masian Beach are the Yeongjong pair official Incheon tourism highlights. Art, shops, and resort spaces first, then the beach for café time and sunset.
c04.tips: The Incheon Airport Maglev stops at Paradise City Station. Masian is toward Muui-do. Check same-day hours for resort venues.

stops.name: Paradise City
stops.desc: Start with the resort’s public spaces and lobby.

stops.name: Art, shops, venues
stops.desc: Pick open exhibitions, shops, or spa time.

stops.name: Masian Beach
stops.desc: Cross toward Muui-do and walk the shore.

stops.name: Sunset & dinner
stops.desc: Stay for sunset, then eat by the beach.

c05.title: Ganghwa history
c05.summary: A pick for visitors curious about Korean history, temple culture, or the inter-Korean border. Jeondeungsa, Ganghwa’s historic sites, then the Ganghwa Peace Observatory.
c05.route: Jeondeungsa → Ganghwa historic area → Ganghwa Peace Observatory
c05.tips: Distances on Ganghwa are long—rent a car or use taxis. Check Peace Observatory hours and ID rules before you go.

stops.name: Jeondeungsa
stops.desc: Ganghwa’s main temple. Walk the bell pavilion and grounds.

stops.name: Ganghwa lunch
stops.desc: Korean meals near the temple or Onsu-ri.

stops.name: Ganghwa historic area
stops.desc: Dolmens and other heritage sites on the island.

stops.name: Ganghwa Peace Observatory
stops.desc: Look over the Han River estuary toward the north.

stops.name: Finish
stops.desc: Head back toward Ganghwa Bridge before it gets late.

c05.notice: Ganghwa Peace Observatory hours and entry rules can change. Check Incheon tourism and the site notice before you go.

c06.title: Ganghwa nature & coast
c06.summary: A driving day from Jeondeungsa to Dongmak Beach and the Ganghwa shore. Coast cafés, a slow drive, and sunset are the point.
c06.tips: Coast buses are sparse—rent a car or use taxis. Dongmak is known for mudflats and sunset; check the tide.

stops.name: Jeondeungsa
stops.desc: Open the day at the mountain temple.

stops.name: Dongmak Beach
stops.desc: Walk Ganghwa’s southern beach and mudflats.

stops.name: Coast drive
stops.desc: A slow run along Ganghwa’s shore roads.

stops.name: Sunset
stops.desc: Close the day on the Yellow Sea light.

gangwon.intro: Day courses across Seoraksan and Sokcho, Gangneung’s coast, Nami Island and Chuncheon, Daegwallyeong, Yangyang, Donghae–Samcheok, and Cheorwon.

c01.title: Sokcho · Seoraksan
c01.summary: Seoraksan and Gwongeumseong, then Sokcho’s fish market, beach, Oeongchi coastal trail, and Daepo Port—the strongest Gangwon day.
c01.route: Seoraksan → Sokcho Market → Sokcho Beach → Oeongchi → Daepo Port
c01.tips: Check cable-car queues and weather. The market is busy at lunch. Wear walking shoes for Oeongchi.

stops.name: Seoraksan National Park
stops.desc: Start around Sogongwon and the Ulsanbawi area.

stops.name: Cable car · Gwongeumseong
stops.desc: Ride up for ridge and East Sea views.

stops.name: Sokcho Tourist Fish Market
stops.desc: Lunch on raw fish and market snacks.

stops.name: Oeongchi coastal trail
stops.desc: Follow the cliffside path above the waves.

stops.name: Daepo Port
stops.desc: Finish with harbor views and dinner.

c02.title: Gangneung sea · café
c02.summary: Gyeongpo Lake and Beach, Jungang Market, Anmok coffee street, and Gangmun Beach—sea and cafés, not forced history stops.
c02.route: Gyeongpo → Gangneung Jungang Market → Anmok → Gangmun
c02.tips: Anmok is crowded on weekends. Bring a layer for the wind.

stops.name: Gyeongpodae · Gyeongpo Lake
stops.desc: Walk the lake and pavilion area.

stops.name: Jungang Market lunch
stops.desc: Eat Gangneung food in the market lanes.

c03.title: Chuncheon · Nami Island
c03.summary: Nami Island, dakgalbi lunch, the Samaksan lake cable car, Uiam Lake, and downtown Chuncheon.
c03.route: Nami Island → Chuncheon → Samaksan cable car → Uiam Lake
c03.tips: Allow ferry time at Nami. Check cable-car weather closures.

stops.name: Chuncheon dakgalbi lunch
stops.desc: Eat spicy stir-fried chicken in town.

stops.name: Chuncheon downtown
stops.desc: Walk Myeong-dong and the market, then dinner.

c04.title: Pyeongchang · Daegwallyeong
c04.summary: Sheep farm, highland roads, Woljeongsa and the fir-tree path—best for visitors who want nature and snow-country scenery.
c04.tips: Check farm hours and weather. The temple path can be slippery.

stops.name: Daegwallyeong Sheep Farm
stops.desc: See sheep on the highland pasture.

stops.name: Pyeongchang lunch
stops.desc: Eat near the farm or temple.

stops.name: Daegwallyeong area
stops.desc: Drive the ridge for open views.

c05.title: Yangyang surf · coast
c05.summary: Naksansa, Naksan Beach, Hajodae and Surfyy Beach—a Yangyang shoreline day.
c05.route: Naksansa → Naksan Beach → Hajodae → Surfyy Beach
c05.tips: Surf beaches change with season and swell. Time the sunset.

stops.name: Naksansa
stops.desc: Temple and Uisangdae above the East Sea.

stops.name: Naksan Beach
stops.desc: Walk the sand below the temple.

stops.name: Sunset · dinner
stops.desc: Watch the light drop, then eat.

c06.title: Donghae · Samcheok coast
c06.summary: Chuam Candle Rock, Dokjaebi Sky Valley, and Mukho’s Nongol mural alleys.
c06.route: Chuam → Dokjaebi Sky Valley → Mukho Port
c06.tips: Sky Valley is high—skip if you dislike heights. Nongol alleys are steep.

stops.name: Chuam Candle Rock
stops.desc: See the sea stack from the lookout.

stops.name: Chuam Beach
stops.desc: Walk the sand under the rock.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Squid and seafood near Chuam or Mukho.

c07.title: Cheorwon Hantangang · DMZ
c07.summary: Columnar-joint trail, Goseokjeong, and Cheorwon DMZ—Hantangang is on Korea’s tourism 100 list.
c07.tips: DMZ tours need ID, bookings, and run on set days.

stops.name: Hantangang columnar-joint trail
stops.desc: Walk the cliff path above basalt columns.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Makguksu or Korean food near Goseokjeong.

chungcheong.intro: Baekje Gongju and Buyeo, Danyang activities, Daecheon Beach, Taean sunsets, and Daejeon city.

c01.title: Gongju Baekje history
c01.summary: Gongsanseong, Sanseong Market, King Muryeong’s tomb, the Gongju museum, and Jemincheon old town.
c01.route: Gongsanseong → Sanseong Market → Royal tombs → Gongju National Museum → Jemincheon
c01.tips: Check indoor tomb-museum routing. Wear walking shoes on the fortress.

stops.name: Gongsanseong
stops.desc: Walk the Baekje walls above the Geumgang.

stops.name: Jemincheon old town
stops.desc: Walk the stream and downtown alleys.

c02.title: Buyeo Baekje history
c02.summary: Busosanseong, Gungnamji, Buyeo National Museum, and Jeongnimsaji—same era as Gongju, different mood.
c02.route: Busosanseong → Gungnamji → Buyeo National Museum → Jeongnimsaji
c02.tips: Busosanseong has a climb. Gungnamji is best near sunset.

stops.name: Busosanseong
stops.desc: Walk the last Baekje fortress woods.

stops.name: Buyeo National Museum
stops.desc: See the gilt-bronze incense burner and more.

c03.title: Danyang nature · activities
c03.summary: Dodamsambong, Mancheonha Skywalk, the river trail, paragliding or Café San, then Guyeong Market.
c03.route: Dodamsambong → Mancheonha Skywalk → Danyanggang trail → paragliding → market
c03.tips: Skywalk and paragliding need weather and bookings.

stops.name: Dodamsambong
stops.desc: Three river peaks from the lookout.

stops.name: Danyang lunch
stops.desc: Garlic and local stews in town.

stops.name: Paragliding or Café San
stops.desc: Fly or take in the view from Café San.

c04.title: Boryeong Daecheon Beach
c04.summary: Beach, seafood, Sky Bike, cafés, and a West Sea sunset—strong in summer; Mud Festival keeps it famous.
c04.route: Daecheon Beach → Sky Bike → shore → sunset
c04.tips: Summer and festival days are packed. Check Sky Bike hours.

stops.name: Daecheon Beach
stops.desc: Open the day on the West Sea sand.

c05.title: Taean West Sea sunset
c05.summary: Anmyeondo and Kkotji Beach, cafés, and the famous rock sunset—theme the day around sea and light.
c05.route: Anmyeondo → Kkotji Beach → West Sea sunset
c05.tips: Aim for the Halmi/Harabi rocks at sunset. Transit is thin.

stops.name: Anmyeondo forest or Kkotji
stops.desc: Start in the woods or at Kkotji.

stops.name: Kkotji Beach
stops.desc: Walk toward the twin sea rocks.

c06.title: Daejeon city · science
c06.summary: National Science Museum, Expo Hanbit Tower, Seongsimdang and Jungang-ro, then old downtown—useful near Cheongju Airport and KTX.
c06.route: Science Museum → Expo → Seongsimdang → old Daejeon
c06.tips: Seongsimdang queues on weekends. Check museum hours.

stops.name: Daejeon lunch
stops.desc: Kalguksu or Korean food near Expo.

stops.name: Seongsimdang · Jungang-ro
stops.desc: Famous bread, then the main street.

jeolla.intro: Jeonju Hanok Village, Yeosu night sea, Suncheon Bay, Damyang bamboo, Boseong tea, and Mokpo’s modern port streets.

c01.title: Jeonju Hanok Village
c01.summary: Village, Gyeonggijeon, bibimbap, Jeondong Cathedral, Omokdae, hanok cafés, and Nambu Market—the first Jeolla pick.
c01.route: Hanok Village → Gyeonggijeon → Jeondong Cathedral → Omokdae → Nambu Market
c01.tips: Rent hanbok in the morning. Weekends are packed.

stops.name: Hanok café · craft
stops.desc: Tea or a short traditional workshop.

c02.title: Yeosu sea · night views
c02.summary: Odongdo, seafood, cable car, Dolsan Park, Yi Sun-sin Square, Nangman pocha, and the night sea.
c02.route: Odongdo → cable car → Dolsan Park → Yi Sun-sin Square → night sea
c02.tips: Cable-car waits run long. Pocha streets open later.

stops.name: Dolsan Park
stops.desc: City and sea from the hill.

c03.title: Suncheon garden · wetland
c03.summary: Suncheon Bay National Garden, the wetland, Yongsan Observatory, and sunset—the nature day in Jeolla.
c03.route: National Garden → Suncheon Bay wetland → Yongsan Observatory
c03.tips: Garden and wetland sit apart; plan transfer time.

c04.title: Damyang bamboo
c04.summary: Juknokwon, Gwanbangjerim, tteokgalbi, the metasequoia road, cafés, and Metaprovence.
c04.tips: Use the pedestrian side of the tree road.

c05.title: Boseong tea · coast
c05.summary: Green-tea terraces, a tea café, then Yulpo Beach—easy to photograph.
c05.tips: Follow field photo rules. Yulpo can be windy.

c06.title: Mokpo modern streets · sea
c06.summary: Modern historic district, marine cable car, Yudalsan, Gatbawi and Peace Plaza, seafood dinner.
c06.route: Modern streets → cable car → Yudalsan → Peace Plaza
c06.tips: Yudalsan is a climb. Cable cars pause in wind.

busan.intro: Haeundae and Gwangalli, Gamcheon and Jagalchi, Songdo and Yeongdo, Haedong Yonggungsa in Gijang, and Seomyeon–Jeonpo.

c01.title: Haeundae · Cheongsapo · Gwangalli
c01.summary: The first-visit Busan day: Haeundae, Dongbaekseom, Blueline Park, Cheongsapo observatory, Gwangalli night.
c01.tips: Check Blueline waits. Gwangandaegyo looks best from the beach at night.

stops.name: Dongbaekseom · The Bay 101
stops.desc: Camellia island and Marine City views.

stops.name: Lunch
stops.desc: Milmyeon or raw fish in Haeundae.

stops.name: Cheongsapo observatory
stops.desc: Cliff lookout over the East Sea.

c02.title: Gamcheon · Jagalchi · Nampo
c02.summary: Culture village, fish market, BIFF Square, Gukje Market, Yongdusan, Nampo—old Busan in one day.
c02.route: Gamcheon → Jagalchi → BIFF Square → Gukje Market → Yongdusan → Nampo
c02.tips: Gamcheon is steep. Jagalchi peaks at lunch.

stops.name: Jagalchi Market lunch
stops.desc: Fish and seafood in the market.

c03.title: Songdo · Yeongdo coast
c03.summary: Songdo Beach, marine cable car, Amnam Park, Huinnyeoul Village, Yeongdo cafés.
c03.route: Songdo Beach → cable car → Amnam Park → Huinnyeoul → Yeongdo
c03.tips: Cable cars pause in wind. Huinnyeoul alleys are steep and narrow.

c04.title: Gijang · Haedong Yonggungsa
c04.summary: Temple in the waves, Gijang coast, Osiria, cafés, sunset.
c04.route: Haedong Yonggungsa → Gijang coast → Osiria → coast café
c04.tips: Go early to the temple. Sunset is best on the Gijang shore.

c05.title: Yeongdo focus
c05.summary: Taejongdae, Huinnyeoul, Jeolyeong coastal trail, cafés, Busan Port night—slow sea day.
c05.route: Taejongdae → Huinnyeoul → Jeolyeong trail → Yeongdo café
c05.tips: Choose the Danubi train or walking paths at Taejongdae.

stops.name: Taejongdae
stops.desc: Cliffs and lighthouse at Yeongdo’s tip.

c06.title: Seomyeon · Jeonpo local
c06.summary: Seomyeon, Jeonpo cafés and shops, shopping, dinner, and night streets—how younger Busan actually hangs out.
c06.tips: Jeonpo is spread out. Nights crowd Seomyeon’s underground mall.

gyeongsang.intro: Day courses across Gyeongbuk, Gyeongnam, Daegu, and Ulsan—Gyeongju, Andong Hahoe, Tongyeong, Geoje Oedo, Pohang, Daegu, Ulsan, and Haeinsa. Busan has its own tab.

c01.title: Gyeongju Silla
c01.summary: Bulguksa, lunch on Hwangnidan-gil, Daereungwon, Cheomseongdae, Gyochon and Woljeonggyo, then Donggung and Wolji at night.
c01.route: Bulguksa → Hwangnidan lunch → Daereungwon → Cheomseongdae → Gyochon · Woljeonggyo → Donggung · Wolji
c01.tips: Bulguksa is quieter early. Check Donggung night hours. Bus and taxi in town.

stops.name: Bulguksa
stops.desc: Walk the compound; Seokguram is a separate ticket uphill.

stops.name: Hwangnidan lunch
stops.desc: Ssambap or Korean food in hanok lanes.

stops.name: Gyochon · Woljeonggyo
stops.desc: Hanok lanes and the rebuilt bridge.

c02.title: Andong Hahoe
c02.summary: Buyongdae overlook, Hahoe Village, lunch, the mask museum, Byeongsan Seowon, and Woryeonggyo. Best by car.
c02.route: Buyongdae → Hahoe → lunch → mask museum → Byeongsan Seowon → Woryeonggyo → dinner
c02.tips: Hahoe charges admission. Byeongsan Seowon is a drive from the village. Woryeonggyo is beautiful after dark.

stops.name: Byeongsan Seowon
stops.desc: Mandaeru hall and the river academy.

c03.title: Tongyeong
c03.summary: Tongyeong cable car and Mireuksan views, Jungang Market lunch, Dongpirang, Gangguan harbor, and Yi Sun-sin Park.
c03.route: Cable car → Mireuksan → market lunch → Dongpirang → Gangguan → Yi Sun-sin Park → dinner
c03.tips: Cable-car waits are common. Dongpirang is steep. Chungmu gimbap is the classic lunch.

c04.title: Geoje Oedo
c04.summary: Cruise to Haegeumgang and Oedo Botania, Geoje lunch, then Windy Hill and Sinseondae. Oedo boats depend on weather.
c04.route: Pier → Haegeumgang → Oedo Botania → lunch → Windy Hill → Sinseondae → dinner
c04.tips: Oedo boats cancel in bad weather—check the day’s sailings. A rental car helps on Geoje’s coast.
c04.notice: Oedo Botania boats cancel or change route in high waves, fog, or wind. Check the operator before you leave.

c05.title: Pohang Space Walk
c05.summary: Jukdo Market, lunch, Yeongildae Beach, Space Walk, a coast café, and Yeongildae night views.
c05.route: Jukdo Market → lunch → Yeongildae Beach → Space Walk → café → night views
c05.tips: Space Walk has height/health limits and queues. Jukdo is liveliest in the morning. Bus from Pohang Station.

stops.name: Space Walk
stops.desc: The slide lookout at Hwanho Park.

stops.name: Coast café
stops.desc: A rest with a sea view.

c06.title: Pohang Homigot · Guryongpo
c06.summary: Homigot, Guryongpo Japanese house street, lunch, the port, a coast café, and back to Pohang. Best by car.
c06.route: Homigot → Japanese houses → lunch → Guryongpo Port → café → back to Pohang
c06.tips: Homigot is a sunrise spot—mornings can be busy. Guryongpo alleys and parking are tight. Buses are infrequent.

stops.name: Homigot
stops.desc: The Hand of Harmony and Korea’s eastern tip.

stops.name: Café · coast
stops.desc: A rest with a sea view.

c07.title: Daegu
c07.summary: Seomun Market, Daegu lunch, the modern-culture alley, Dongseong-ro, Apsan Observatory, and night views. Easy by metro.
c07.route: Seomun Market → lunch → modern alley → Dongseong-ro → Apsan Observatory → night views
c07.tips: Seomun is a morning market. Dongseong-ro is walkable. Apsan has a cable car and buses.

c08.title: Ulsan
c08.summary: Taehwa River National Garden, lunch, Daewangam Park, Ilsan Beach, a coast walk, and dinner.
c08.route: Taehwa Garden → lunch → Daewangam Park → Ilsan Beach → coast walk → dinner
c08.tips: Garden and Daewangam are apart—bus or taxi. Daewangam has a long coastal walk.

c09.title: Hapcheon Haeinsa
c09.summary: Haeinsa, the Tripitaka Koreana, a Gayasan walk, and a café rest. Temple day only. The finish has no photo.
c09.route: Haeinsa → lunch → Tripitaka · temple → Gayasan walk → café → finish
c09.tips: Janggyeong Panjeon limits indoor photos. Mountain-vegetable sets are the classic lunch. Hapcheon is rental car or intercity bus.

stops.name: Gayasan walk
stops.desc: A short forest path around the temple.

stops.name: Finish
stops.desc: Back toward Daegu or Gwangju before dark.

jeju.intro: Day courses around Jeju—Seongsan and Udo, Hyeopjae and Aewol, Seogwipo falls, Jungmun, Hallasan, Jeju City markets, eastern oreum, and Sanbangsan. Pick a title to see the intro, route, and timetable.

c01.title: Seongsan · east Jeju
c01.summary: Seongsan Ilchulbong and Seopjikoji, lunch, Aqua Planet or a café, Gwangchigi Beach, and dinner around Seongsan.
c01.route: Seongsan → Seopjikoji → lunch → Aqua Planet / café → Gwangchigi → dinner
c01.tips: Ilchulbong is quieter in the morning. The summit is steep stairs. Check Aqua Planet hours.

stops.name: Aqua Planet or café
stops.desc: The aquarium or an ocean-view café.

c02.title: Udo day trip
c02.summary: Seongsan Port to Udo, a coast loop, lunch, Geommeolle and Hagosudong, peanut ice cream, back to Seongsan.
c02.route: Seongsan Port → Udo → coast loop → lunch → Geommeolle → café ice cream → back
c02.tips: Udo ferries cancel in high waves. E-carts and scooters are easiest on the island. Don’t miss the last boat.
c02.notice: Udo ferries can cancel for swell, fog, or wind. Check Seongsan Port the same day and do not miss the last return boat.

c03.title: Hyeopjae · west Jeju
c03.summary: Hyeopjae and Geumneung beaches, Hallim lunch, Osulloc Tea Museum, a west-coast café, and sunset.
c03.route: Hyeopjae → Geumneung → Hallim lunch → Osulloc → café → sunset
c03.tips: Hyeopjae faces Biyangdo with emerald water. Osulloc may charge admission. Sunset is best on the coast road.

c04.title: Aewol · Handam
c04.summary: Aewol coast road and Handam walk, lunch, café street, Gwakji Beach, sunset, and dinner.
c04.route: Aewol coast → Handam walk → lunch → cafés → Gwakji Beach → sunset → dinner
c04.tips: Handam has one-way traffic and tight parking. Café street queues on weekends. A rental car helps.

stops.name: Aewol coast road
stops.desc: A slow drive by the sea.

c05.title: Seogwipo waterfalls
c05.summary: Jeongbang Falls, Seogwipo town and Olle Market lunch, Cheonjiyeon Falls, Saeyeongyo and Saeseom, then the Seogwipo coast and dinner.
c05.route: Jeongbang → downtown → Olle Market lunch → Cheonjiyeon → Saeyeongyo · Saeseom → coast → dinner
c05.tips: Jeongbang falls into the sea. Check Cheonjiyeon evening hours. Downtown is walkable.

c06.title: Jungmun
c06.summary: Jusangjeolli and Jungmun Beach, lunch, Yeomiji Botanical Garden or a museum, the resort belt, a coast café, and dinner.
c06.route: Jusangjeolli → Jungmun Beach → lunch → Yeomiji / museum → resort → café → dinner
c06.tips: Jusangjeolli has strong waves. The resort belt is large—shuttle or taxi. Stay in Jungmun; don’t mix other sightseeing.

stops.name: Coast café
stops.desc: A rest with a sea view.

c07.title: Hallasan
c07.summary: A hiking-only day. Dawn start at Seongpanak or Gwaneumsa, summit or Witseoreum, descent, then black-pork dinner. Do not mix other sightseeing.
c07.route: Trailhead → summit / Witseoreum → descent → black-pork dinner
c07.tips: Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa require reservations. Pick Witseoreum instead of the summit if weather or fitness is limited. Do not add other sights.

stops.name: Black-pork dinner
stops.desc: Recover at a restaurant below the mountain.

c07.notice: Hallasan Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa trails need advance booking. Same-day walk-up may be refused. Check national-park notices.

c08.title: Jeju City · markets
c08.summary: Yongduam and Yongyeon valley, lunch, Jejummok Gwandea and old downtown, Dongmun Market, Tapdong shore, and market-food dinner.
c08.route: Yongduam → Yongyeon → lunch → Jejummok Gwandea → Dongmun Market → Tapdong → market food
c08.tips: Yongduam is a short stop. Dongmun Market is best in the evening. City buses and taxis are enough.

stops.name: Yongyeon valley · coast
stops.desc: A short gorge and shore walk.

c09.title: East forest · oreum
c09.summary: Bijarim Forest, Woljeongri Beach lunch, Yongnuni Oreum or a nearby oreum, Sehwa Beach, and an east-coast café dinner. Best by car.
c09.route: Bijarim → Woljeongri Beach → lunch → Yongnuni Oreum → Sehwa Beach → café dinner
c09.tips: Bijarim’s dirt path is slippery. Oreum walks depend on wind and fitness. Woljeongri cafés are crowded.

stops.name: East café · dinner
stops.desc: Finish at a café or restaurant.

c10.title: Sanbangsan · southwest
c10.summary: Sanbangsan and Yongmeori Coast, lunch, Songaksan, Sagye coast, and a southwest sunset. Best by car.
c10.route: Sanbangsan → Yongmeori Coast → lunch → Songaksan → Sagye coast → sunset
c10.tips: Yongmeori can close in high waves or tide. Songaksan is a short climb. Sunset is classic at Sagye or Songak.

stops.name: Sanbangsan
stops.desc: The cliff mountain and Sanbanggul cave.
